title: Naturality of condensed finite-to-Qbar exchange comparisons
statement: Fix the coefficient rings, bounded constructible categories, scalar extension T, and the four specified comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-comparisons]. For separated finite-type schemes over a field k of prime characteristic different from ℓ and k-morphisms f:X→Y, g:Y'→Y, f':X'→Y', g':X'→X forming any commutative square sq, let B_A be the unit-square-counit bounded constructible exchange of [def-weil-pbc-condensed-e-module-category]. For each K in C_E(X), S_K followed by B_Ω(T_X K) equals T_Y'(B_E(K)) followed by U_K. No properness, Cartesianity, or invertibility of push comparisons or exchange maps is assumed.

proof.text: Expand pullIsoOfComapIso and pushHomOfComapIso from the same derived restriction/direct-image comparison. Conjugation along the composite adjunction is successive transposition; cancellation of inverse transpositions shows that the push comparison is the pull/push mate of the inverse pull comparison. Its adjunct is the inverse pull comparison followed by scalar extension of the counit.

The pull comparisons respect inverse-image composition. Underived, both routes multiply the same nested scalar tensors, so tensor balancing and sheafification identify them. Exact pullback and flat scalar extension descend these equalities termwise to the derived category; the defined derived comparisons are the conjugates of the restriction/direct-image comparisons. This gives the commuting pullback cube T(theta_E), alpha_g′, l_g′(alpha_f) = alpha_f′, l_f′(alpha_g), theta_Omega(T), including substitution by the square commutativity proof.

Apply the mate-pasting identities mateEquiv_hcomp and mateEquiv_vcomp (or mateEquiv_square) to that cube. The mates of theta are the specified unit-square-counit exchanges, and the edge mates are precisely the push comparisons from the first step. The resulting pasted equality is S_K then B_Omega(TK) = T(B_E(K)) then U_K. Restriction along fully faithful inclusions preserves the adjunction units, counits and composition comparisons, giving the displayed bounded constructible equality. No map is inverted except the pull comparison.
